description:
UNVERIFIED - A/B ONLY. The "widen the input buffer" route, filed under the repo's UNVERIFIED-AB convention because the mechanism is only half proven. Apply on its own, play one match, and if you cannot tell, revert it.

WHAT IS KNOWN (b-DISASSEMBLY). The pad layer keeps a HISTORY RING, not a single frame: 0x14431a5b0(padHistory, framesAgo) returns the button bitmask for a past frame, and both query helpers walk it - 0x14430f9b0(pad, button, framesAgo) is "was there a rising edge that many frames back", and 0x144310490(pad, button, start, window, maxGap, ...) scans backwards over a window looking for a press. match::pad::ThinkUnitBase::vf17 - the shared "was this button pressed?" used by the button ThinkUnits - calls 0x144310490 with start = 2 ('lea r8d,[rax+2]' at 0x1440d8035) and window = 6 ('lea r9d,[rax+6]' at 0x1440d802d). Both ring walkers clamp at index 0x63, so the ring itself is 99 frames deep - about 1.65 s at 60 fps. Separately: NO RTTI-named method in match::pad:: or match::ai:: reads the current anime action kind at animePlayer+0xad0 anywhere in the image. So input IS sampled and IS turned into requests while you are locked in a stagger; it is the anime layer that throws the request away.

WHAT THIS PACK CHANGES. The 6 becomes 12 - one byte. A button press is then still visible to ThinkUnitBase::vf17 for twice as long, so a press made during a lock has twice the chance of still counting on the frame the lock lifts.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN (c-INFERRED, and this is why it is quarantined). It was NOT established that a request refused by the anime gate is re-issued on the next frame from this history, rather than consumed and dropped on the frame it was made. If the ThinkUnit latches "already handled" state (several of them do keep a +0x48 style latch), widening the window buys nothing. It was also not established that 6 is a frame count rather than an index into something else, though every other argument to that helper is a frame count.

RISK IF IT DOES WORK. A wider press window makes every button in the game slightly stickier, not just the ones you care about: expect occasional double-actions, a shot going off later than you meant, or a pass firing after you thought you had let go. That is the thing to watch for. Start at 12; do not go higher.

WHO IT AFFECTS: human pads only. ThinkUnitBase is the human input side; the AI does not go through it.

COLLISIONS: none. 0x1440d802d is 448D4806 in both the INSTALLED image and eFootball.exe.PRISTINE (verified this pass).

REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/input-button-window-wider-UNVERIFIED-AB.json

patches.name: shared button-press history window 6 -> 12 frames - UNVERIFIED
patches.note: lea r9d,[rax+6] -> lea r9d,[rax+0xc] in match::pad::ThinkUnitBase::vf17 (0x1440d8000); rax is 0 here so r9d is the literal window passed to the pad-history scanner 0x144310490. Same length, no cell written.
